name: Elimination of crossings
summary: Between the legs of two white vertices merged by a W-node, a fermionic crossing is an ordinary swap.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

Rule X of Hadzihasanovic's first complete ZW-calculus: two white vertices whose outputs are merged by a black monoid (a W-node), with their inputs interleaved through a fermionic crossing, equal the same diagram with an ordinary swap. It is used to eliminate crossings when rewriting to normal form.

In the 2015 paper the white structures are a ternary white vertex with a binary white vertex on its output, i.e. two Z-spiders with phase $\pi$, which fuse to the phase-free Z-spiders drawn here.
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator
